Q01.text: How well do the last four weeks reflect the cat’s usual behavior?
Q01.help: Describe the last four weeks, or the shorter time you have known the cat. Do not mix behavior before a change with behavior afterwards.

options.usual: I have known the cat for at least four weeks; this period is usual for them
options.changed: Behavior or living conditions have noticeably changed recently
options.health: This is a period of illness, treatment or noticeable mobility difficulties
options.short: I have known the cat for less than four weeks
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q02.text: Who, apart from adult caregivers, lives with the cat or regularly visits the home?
Q02.help: Select the relevant groups. Children’s names, exact ages and personal details are not needed.

options.other_animals: Other animals, such as rabbits, birds or rodents
options.deferred: I will fill this in later

Q03.text: Whose presence is most clearly associated with a noticeable difference in the cat’s behavior?
Q03.help: Compare only naturally occurring situations. A difference may also mean more play or contact. Choose several groups if it concerns more than one.

options.none: I have not noticed such a difference
options.other_animals: Other animals, such as rabbits, birds or rodents
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q04.text: How often does the cat start playing on their own when awake and with toys available?
Q04.help: For example, chasing a ball or playing with an object. No toys or no opportunity means unobserved, rather than never.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q05.text: How often does the cat start playing when you calmly offer a familiar toy while they are awake?
Q05.help: Describe starting play, not the length of a session. Exclude waking the cat, persistent prompting or play interrupted by housemates.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q06.text: How often does the cat move away or hide when a familiar housemate walks past without approaching them?
Q06.help: Exclude touching, lifting, chasing and simply making room to pass. If responses differ clearly between housemates, choose context dependent.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q07.text: How often does the cat stop what they are doing and move away or hide after an ordinary household sound?
Q07.help: For example, a cupboard closing or a chair moving. Merely turning the head does not count. Exclude alarms, building work and deliberate startling.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q08.text: How often does the cat approach you for friendly contact outside feeding time?
Q08.help: For example, approaching to rub against you or give a head bump. Both questions in this pair describe contact with you, the respondent, rather than a family average.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q09.text: How often does the cat choose to rest close to you when a comfortable place farther away is also available?
Q09.help: Close means within arm’s reach; sitting on your lap is not required. Describe free choice without holding the cat or using food.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q10.text: How often does the cat initiate friendly contact with {other_cat}?
Q10.help: For example, approaching to rub against or groom that cat. Eating nearby or occupying the same sofa is not enough. Both relationship questions concern the same other cat.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q11.text: How often does the cat increase distance when {other_cat} comes nearby?
Q11.help: For example, leaving the room, changing route or moving higher to avoid an approach. Exclude taking turns chasing during play and simply walking past.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q12.text: How often does the cat independently approach a new, stationary object to look at or sniff it?
Q12.help: Only consider available objects that naturally appeared at home. Exclude toys moved by people and objects containing food. Not approaching does not prove fear.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q13.text: How often does the cat independently explore a newly accessible place in the familiar home?
Q13.help: For example, a previously closed area or an empty shelf, if this has already happened. Exclude placing the cat there, food lures or someone blocking access.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q14.text: How often does the cat pause to inspect a familiar meal before taking the first bite?
Q14.help: Describe a noticeable pause to look or sniff at the bowl, at the usual mealtime without interference. Exclude eating speed and new food trials. If such calm meals do not occur, choose no opportunity.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q15.text: At what height does the cat usually rest when freely choosing a place?
Q15.help: Describe choice, not jumping ability. Elevated includes a seat, furniture back, windowsill or shelf. The scale records frequency of choosing above-floor places, not height in centimeters.

options.mostly_elevated: Mostly on furniture, windowsills or shelves
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q16.text: How sheltered are the places the cat usually chooses to rest?
Q16.help: Sheltered includes a den, under furniture or behind a plant; open includes an exposed rug or open shelf. A furniture back can be both elevated and open.

options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q17.text: What alternative resting places are genuinely accessible to the cat?
Q17.help: One answer describes the available choices. Consider closed doors, difficulty reaching a place, and people or animals occupying or blocking it.

options.both: Choice of both height and shelter: low and elevated, sheltered and open
options.height_only: Choice of height, but only one type of shelter
options.cover_only: Choice of shelter, but only one height level
options.neither: Only one type of place is accessible
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

Q18.text: How often does the cat relax their body and fall asleep calmly in their chosen resting places?
Q18.help: Describe a repeated pattern. Lying still alone is not enough. Remaining watchful, crouched or soon leaving does not count as calmly falling asleep. This is not a separate stress diagnosis.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.unobserved: There was no opportunity to observe this
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

F_TARGET.text: Which other cat will you describe in this short interview?
F_TARGET.help: Choose one cat or enter a temporary name. We do not choose automatically. The remaining relationships will stay undescribed.

F_CONTEXT.text: What mainly changes in the cat’s behavior around {group}?
F_CONTEXT.help: Choose the clearest pattern, or several changes. An association with someone’s presence does not establish a cause.

options.withdraw: Moves away or hides more often
options.space: Changes resting places or movement routes
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

F_SPACE.text: Which description best matches the use of resting places?
F_SPACE.help: This clarifies the conditions. It adds no caution points and does not replace observations of freely chosen calm rest.

options.access: Access to other places is limited or blocked
options.retreat: Mainly goes there after moving away from someone
options.mobility: I notice difficulty climbing or jumping
options.varied: Both calm rest and retreat occur
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

F_VARIATION.text: The answers about {axis} differ. What might explain this?
F_VARIATION.help: Both answers can be accurate. Do not force them to agree.

options.different_contexts: The situations differ, and the behavior differs with them
options.varies_same_context: The behavior varies even in similar conditions
options.deferred: I will observe and answer later

relationshipNotes.affiliation_and_distancing_coexist: Friendly contact and increasing distance coexist in this relationship.
relationshipNotes.little_affiliation_and_frequent_distanci: In this relationship, initiating friendly contact was reported infrequently and increasing distance often.
